author: sonnet
label: pilot-junior-fix-01
changes: Replaced 'the brief' wording with 'the request' and added a 'Terms and sources' section separating fixed rules from choices made in the plan (Q1).
Added an 'Existing building blocks' table naming each function, where it lives, and what is new to build; named the three files explicitly (Q2, Q8).
Step 1: row_count is now read from the replica, with the reasoning and an open question about whether the replica holds reports (Q8).
Step 0: added item 6 for the report-name lookup and a user_id-based report.view check usable without a request (Q7).
Step 3: POST response now includes filters; stale check clarified as applying only to rows with no job_id; added the crash-after-enqueue-before-job_id case and why it is harmless (Q3, Q4).

Step 4: stated that the handler does not set failed on attempt 3 and only on_final_failure does; described the worker-killed path ending in on_final_failure; added the crash between complete_multipart and done leading to a full rebuild; folded the soft deadline into the streaming loop; explained that filters are validated by iter_report_rows and that the permission check uses the stored user_id (Q4-Q7).
Step 7: the POST response now seeds the status display before polling begins (Q3).
Step 5: noted the report name source; Step 8: added a worker-death check; open questions: added queue delivery guarantee, replica/reports table, permission-check callability and report name column.
Step 5a: update now requires state='running' and the job reloads the row; if it is not done the job stops and sends no email (fixes the failed-row-still-emails gap).

Step 4 part 5: added a between-pages cancellation check so a job whose row was marked failed aborts its upload and stops; Step 3 failure text now explains the overlap with a second job and why keys cannot collide.
Step 3: replaced the 2-minute stale check with a named Dead-row rule adding a 2-hour updated_at backstop for lost jobs or an unrecorded final failure; Step 6 and the open questions point to it.
Step 4 failure: said what happens if the set-back-to-queued update itself fails (log, re-raise original error, row stays running).
Step 0 item 1 and open questions: filters and cols are stored as text exactly as received, and their encoding and parser location are flagged as unknown.
Steps 1 and 2: stated the page uses fetch and branches on Content-Type (text/csv vs JSON), and shows an error when the stream is cut.
Step 7 and How the pieces fit: made explicit that the emailed link is the only way to get the file and that clicking again starts a new export.
Step 8: added checks for a row marked dead mid-job and for click handling; renumbered the rest.
Terms and sources: listed the 2-hour check and the fetch choice among the plan's own decisions.

Added a general rule in 'How the pieces fit': every write to a report_exports row names its export_id and the allowed current states, and a zero-row result means someone else moved it. Why: Q15 and Q16 showed unguarded writes.
Step 4 part 3: marking running is now conditional (WHERE export_id AND state IN queued/running); zero rows changed means return without uploading. Why: Q15, a failed row must not be revived.
Step 4 Failure: the set-back-to-queued update is now conditional on state='running' and ignored if it changes nothing. Why: Q15.
Step 6: on_final_failure now loads and updates by payload export_id plus state, sends the email only if the update changed a row. Why: Q16, it could have failed a newer export.
Step 3 dead-row update and Step 5a update now state their export_id and state conditions explicitly; Step 5a also sets updated_at. Why: consistency with the new rule.
Step 1: specified the POST as a fetch with a JSON body {filters, cols} and that the caller is identified by the same session credentials as the rows API (assumed, unverified). Why: Q17.
Step 0 item 1 and open questions: removed the stale reference to URL examples, added open questions on filters encoding inconsistency and on how the rows API identifies the caller. Why: Q17.
Step 8: added checks 8 (old export's final failure leaves a newer export alone) and 9 (failed-before-start job does nothing); renumbered the rest. Why: Q15, Q16.
Step 1 action 1: said the report.view check must find the report's workspace and reuse the rows API's code, noting the lookup and signature are unknown (Q18).
Open questions: added how report.view finds the workspace and what it takes as input (Q18).
Step 3 action 2, Notes, and Step 7 part 2: stated that when an existing export with different filters is returned, the page compares filters and shows a message, and starts no new export (Q19).
Step 7 Data moves: defined 'most recent' as latest created_at for the user and report, and said the GET reads from the primary and why (Q20).
Step 0 item 2: added a plain index on (user_id, report_id, created_at) for the status lookup (Q20).
Terms and sources: listed reading the status endpoint from the primary among the plan's own choices.
Step 8 checks 10 and 13: added the different-filters message check and noted report_exports uses the primary.
Building blocks table: noted the rows API checks report.view on the report's workspace.
holes: Q7: When the job reads filters and cols from the row, does it re-validate them, and does the 'report.view' re-check in step 2 use the row's user_id with no live request? How is the report name for the email obtained? (author: Filters and cols are not re-validated by the handler itself; they were validated at click time and iter_report_rows applies the same validation and would raise if they no longer fit (decided, now in Step 4). The report.view re-check uses the row's user_id with no request; I do not know whether the existing check can be called that way, so Step 0 item 6 says to wrap it if needed and it is an open question. The report name comes from the reports table by report_id; I do not know the column name (assumed reports.name) and have marked it to confirm.)

Q8: What is `row_count` stored on exactly, and what does 'the three files' refer to in 'Existing facts this plan relies on (from the three files)'? (author: row_count is a column on the reports table: the total unfiltered number of rows, rewritten each night (reports_page.md). 'The three files' meant the existing descriptions reports_page.md, jobs.py and storage.py; I now name them in the 'Existing building blocks' section. reports_page.md does not say which database holds the reports table. I chose to read row_count from the replica, which is safe under either reading of the replica-only rule, but whether the replica carries the reports table is unknown and listed as an open question (fall back to the primary if not).)

Q11: What do filters and cols look like (strings, JSON, query-string text)? Which code turns them into a database query, and does it run on the replica? (author: The page URL carries filters as query values (e.g. status=open&region=EU) and cols as a comma list (cols=date,customer,amount); reports_page.md does not show the exact encoding of the rows API 'filters' parameter or where the parser code lives. The plan stores both as text exactly as received and reuses the rows API's existing parser inside iter_report_rows. Parsing only builds the query; the query itself runs on the read replica. Encoding and parser location are now an open question.)

Q17: How does the page send filters and cols to the POST: in the URL query string, the JSON body, or a form body? And how does the endpoint learn who the caller is? (author: Decided: the page sends a JSON body {"filters": "...", "cols": "..."} with each value being the text it already sends to the rows API; the report id is in the URL path. I chose a body because it avoids URL length and encoding problems and the server keeps the text as received. Unknown: how the caller is identified. reports_page.md does not describe authentication. The plan assumes the fetch sends the same session credentials as the rows API and the endpoint reuses its identification; this is now stated in Step 1 and listed as an open question. Also unknown is the exact filters encoding, already an open question.)

Q18: Step 1 says to check report.view 'on the report's workspace'. Where does the workspace come from: is it a column on the report, and how does the check take it as input? (author: reports_page.md only says the rows API checks report.view "on the report's workspace". It does not say where the workspace comes from or what the check takes as input. I assume the workspace is found from the report (a reference on the reports row), but that is a guess. The plan now says to reuse the rows API's exact check and lookup code rather than write a second one, and lists it as an open question.)
